statement: [DATO, abstract only] The 2015 Science report states that LDH inhibition hyperpolarised neurons, that this was reversed by pyruvate, that seizures were reduced in vivo and that stiripentol is an LDH inhibitor; its concentrations, n, engagement, KATP dependence and any control for stiripentol GABA-A action could not be read (publisher HTTP 403).

[DATO] Deleting Ldha in astrocytes of adult mouse dmPFC lowered extracellular lactate and neuronal firing (13 vs 12 neurons, 3 vs 3 mice) without a change in resting potential or input resistance, and increased depressive-like behaviour: a lactate-side reduction that lowered excitability and was harmful by the authors behavioural readout. [V2 correction: the Vm/Rin null (13 vs 12 neurons) is the GFAP-Cre conditional knockout, which acts in neural progenitors (neurons and astrocytes), not an adult astrocyte-specific deletion; the astrocyte-specific AAV arm (12 vs 13 neurons) reports firing and lactate only]

statement: [DATO] The same paper found no effect of a neuron-targeted (CaMKIIa) Ldha knockdown on lactate, firing (12 vs 15 neurons, 3 vs 3 mice) or behaviour, while knocking down the neuronal lactate transporter MCT2 lowered firing and blocked a lactate rescue: the lactate-side effect in that preparation sits in astrocyte supply and neuronal uptake, not in neuronal LDHA.

statement: [DATO] In P12-16 mouse dentate granule neurons 2 mM R-beta-hydroxybutyrate raised single-channel KATP open probability (peak 3.14 +/- 0.90 percent, 8 patches, vs 1.09 +/- 0.32 percent, 35 patches; basal 1.71 vs 0.46 percent), in cell-attached patches that leave ATP undisturbed; no membrane potential or input resistance was measured.

[DATO calculation by the authors] They estimate that activity-driven KATP opening could add about 30 percent, and BHB about 100 percent, to a resting conductance of 400-500 pS in young high-input-resistance granule cells; this is scaled from two NN414 whole-cell recordings, not measured, and is for a young cell type.
